label: sparse early-sequence conjunction (first token i/j/p, e/f near position 2, steps 4-5)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). It never fires at t<3 or on the delimiter, and almost never at t>=10. Most of its activity is at t=4-5, either in the original phase (orig_idx 3-5) or in the copy phase of short sequences (recall_idx 1-2, mostly L=3-4). It is enriched for sequences that start with j, i or p, have no digits, and have e/f/t two steps back. The input tokens are mostly h, p, i or g. The largest activations are copy-phase steps re-reading the first token (e.g. i j f f <DEL> [i], p j e <DEL> [p]). None of these cues is selective. The best conjunction (first token i/j/p, orig(2) in {e,f}, t in 4..5) reaches only about 5% precision and 17% recall on dev, and broader phase/position predicates reach about 40-58% recall at under 1% precision. It looks like a fine-grained hidden-state conjunction with no compact token-level description.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=j (+4.91), t=4 (+4.05), phase=2 & in_tok=h (+3.66), orig0=i (+3.54), prev2_tok=f (+3.48), prev_tok=w (+3.40). Lower it: correct=1 (-6.07), in_count=0 (-5.49), prev2_tok=i (-2.95), to_go=0 (-2.44).
